newsitem.title: UK: Hepworth extends gain, SBC Warburg positive.
newsitem.headline: Hepworth extends gain, SBC Warburg positive.

text.p: Shares in building products group Hepworth Plc rose to a five-month high on Tuesday, extending Monday's rise as SBC Warburg rated the stock a "buy" with a 300p price target, dealers said.
Hepworth shares were up 10p at 285-1/2 by 0854 GMT, their highest since November last year, in volume of 588,597 shares.
On Monday the stock rose on news that chief executive John Carter had resigned from the company following a lacklustre profit performance.
Analysts at SBC Warburg were not immediately available for comment.
Howard Proctor, analyst at SocGen, also repeated a "buy" on Hepworth, arguing that sentiment was improving towards the stock amid restrucuring hopes.
"The perception of Hepworth as a rather dull, mature business which is poorly focused is slowly changing," Proctor said.

The SocGen analyst cited Hepworth's recent disposal of its refractories division as an example of the company's restructuring efforts, designed to shift the company out of low-growth markets and into more promising fields.
